content.what_it_is: MATLAB script (OSU runup benchmark, BM2), 4-panel extension of plot_ADV_AB.m comparing model vs ADV velocities. Panels: 411 ADV A (labeled 'ADV 1'), 412 ADV B ('ADV 2'), 413 ADV C U-component ('ADV 3'), 414 ADV C V-component ('ADV 3'). sk=2 subsampling, fact=1 (L3-4); figure sized 8x7 in (L6). First time alignment (L8-32): model FSE_BM2_shi_tvd.txt vs WG1.txt peak match, t=t-num_t_shift+exp_t_shift-0.25 (L32). ADV A: VT_A_BM2_shi_tvd.txt + U_Velocity_AverageA.txt (L35-40), plotted in subplot(411) (L42-49: measured demeaned by mean of first 25 samples L43, model vel(:,1)/fact L46, axis [0 47 -2.0 3.5] L49). ADV B: VT_B + U_Velocity_AverageB (L51-56), 'ADV 1' text and legend issued at L57-58 (before subplot 412), subplot(412) plots (L60-69). For C the alignment block is repeated (L73-97) but WITHOUT the -0.25 s correction (L97: t=t-num_t_shift+exp_t_shift). ADV C U: VT_C_BM2_shi_tvd.txt + U_Velocity_AverageC.txt (L100-105), subplot(413) (L107-114). ADV C V: VT_C reloaded + V_Velocity_AverageC.txt (L116-121), subplot(414) plots model vel(:,2) (V component) (L125-135), ylabel 'V (m/s)' (L132), xlabel Time (L135). No writes.

unresolved: Panels A/B use the -0.25 s corrected shift (L32) while the repeated alignment block for C omits it (L97) although both derive from the same files -- inconsistent shifts between panels without explanation.

text('ADV 1') and legend at L57-58 are placed after the B data loads but before subplot(412), so they land on the first axes; panel labels 'ADV 1/2/3' differ from the AB script's 'ADV A/B' naming, and 'ADV 3' appears twice (L122 on axes 413, L133 on 414).

The C alignment block (L73-97) recomputes exactly what L8-32 already computed except the constant; num_shift_ind/exp_shift_ind never used; n=6 overwrites the size() result each time (L37, L53, L102, L118); vel padded to 6 columns though only columns 1-2 are plotted.
V-component comparison (L130) takes model vel(:,2), i.e. column 3 of VT_C_BM2_shi_tvd.txt; the column layout of the VT files is not documented in this script.
